label: Uneasy
summary: The Iran war remained the day's dominant story, with tankers reported hit in the Strait of Hormuz and both Washington and Tehran claiming control of the waterway. Russian attacks killed at least eight people in Ukraine and cut power to a million homes, and Israeli settlers attacked European diplomats in the West Bank. Kenya's Ebola count rose to seven. Cost-of-living protests turned violent across France, and the IMF warned that poorer nations face inflation and war spillovers. There was some good news. Pope Leo returned to the Vatican after cancer surgery, solar power is booming in the Philippines, and Stanford researchers reported reversing coral bleaching at record speed. NASA's Roman telescope is outperforming expectations, and a new drug reversed severe fatty liver disease. The weighted formula gave 41; no editorial adjustment.
